YYM004raeDDyy4eCxuHG.nombre: Jurisprudencia (Jurisprudence): AI for Calculating Guarantees in Amparo (II.2o.C. J/1 K)
YYM004raeDDyy4eCxuHG.resumen: Jurisprudencia (Jurisprudence) by reiteration of the Segundo Tribunal Colegiado en Materia Civil del Segundo Circuito (Second Civil Panel of the Second Circuit, State of Mexico): AI tools may validly be employed in judicial proceedings to calculate the amount of guarantees in amparo (Mexican constitutional relief proceedings), without replacing the work of judges, facilitating and improving the efficiency of justice administration. Published in the Gaceta del SJF (Semanario Judicial de la Federación Gazette, Book 5, January 2026, p. 597) on January 9, 2026, and binding as of January 12, 2026. Derives from the tesis aislada (isolated judicial thesis) II.2o.C.8 K (11a.), reg. 2031009 (first appearance of "artificial intelligence" in the Semanario Judicial de la Federación). It is the judicial counterpoint to the package of 14 initiatives by Sen. Dorantes (July 2026): the Judicial Branch has already recognized through precedent AI as an auxiliary tool under human supervision.
YYM004raeDDyy4eCxuHG.hechos: Multiple parties filed recursos de queja (administrative complaints) and recursos de revisión (review proceedings) in the suspension incident to challenge the amount of guarantees set by Juzgados de Distrito (District Courts), arguing that their determination lacked objective parameters or failed to consider the personal characteristics and economic capacity of the complainant.
YYM004raeDDyy4eCxuHG.elementoIA: Use of artificial intelligence tools as support for auxiliary calculations (amounts of guarantees in amparo): value updates, application of interest rates, and assessment of procedural timeframes. AI is not part of the core decision-making process; it provides step-by-step traceability, reduces errors, and standardizes precedents, while preserving the motivation required by artículo 16 constitucional (Constitutional Article 16).

mvUFbQG4Vou8zHVKDKBs.nombre: IPN Deepfakes Case — Digital Violence Proceedings, Without Final Judgment
mvUFbQG4Vou8zHVKDKBs.resumen: Emblematic deepfakes-with-AI case in Mexico, STILL WITHOUT BINDING PRECEDENT. Diego N., a former IPN student, was accused of using AI to alter intimate photographs of classmates. In late 2024, he was ACQUITTED of digital violence charges involving AI due to lack of evidence; that proceeding (and several related investigation files) remain pending. In May 2025, he received a 5-year prison sentence, but for HUMAN TRAFFICKING (child sexual abuse material storage) — a SEPARATE case, NOT for the AI manipulation. Therefore, the legal question regarding AI deepfakes still lacks a binding resolution: this case file documents an ONGOING case, not a precedent.
mvUFbQG4Vou8zHVKDKBs.elementoIA: Use of generative AI algorithms to create pornographic deepfakes from real photographs of students. The legal question of AI manipulation remains unresolved (see summary).

yZmMwc4LtTSwjxirJLuZ.nombre: Avatar Virtual INDAUTOR Case (Intellectual Property and AI)
yZmMwc4LtTSwjxirJLuZ.resumen: A landmark precedent case addressing whether a digital work called "Avatar Virtual," created through artificial intelligence (Leonardo platform), could be registered for copyright. The SCJN (Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación) unanimously ruled that works created exclusively by AI cannot be registered under copyright law in Mexico, affirming that authorship is reserved to human beings.
yZmMwc4LtTSwjxirJLuZ.elementoIA: The Leonardo AI platform was used to generate a virtual avatar trained on photographs of the applicant. The case directly examines the registrability of works autonomously generated by AI.

AAA2mbIKed25Hs8Nkv9f.nombre: Case: Digital Violence and Criminal Definition of AI (Sinaloa)
AAA2mbIKed25Hs8Nkv9f.resumen: The SCJN validated the reform to the Código Penal de Sinaloa (Penal Code of Sinaloa) that criminalizes the creation of false sexual content (deepfakes) using artificial intelligence. The Court determined that the definition of AI employed by the local legislature ('programs that offer automatic adjustments') is constitutional and sufficiently clear (meets the requirement of taxativity, the legality principle requiring penal laws to be precisely defined) to understand the prohibited conduct, without need for a complex technical definition.
AAA2mbIKed25Hs8Nkv9f.hechos: On February 12, 2024, Sinaloa reformed Article 185 Bis C of its Código Penal de Sinaloa (Penal Code of Sinaloa) to punish anyone who manipulates intimate images with AI. The Ejecutivo Federal (Federal Executive Branch) challenged the norm arguing that the definition of AI was vague, imprecise ('automatic adjustments') and technically deficient, which generated legal uncertainty (the lack of taxativity—the legality principle requiring laws to be clearly defined) by confusing AI with simple editing filters.
AAA2mbIKed25Hs8Nkv9f.elementoIA: The debate centered on the challenged legal definition: 'Artificial Intelligence shall be understood as applications, programs or technology that analyze photographs, audio or video and offer automatic adjustments to alter or modify them.' The Court concluded that this operative definition is valid for criminal law because it allows the average citizen to understand that it is prohibited to use automated software to falsify reality.

D0YWuWHjUKj45sISuZmW.nombre: Case on Ethical Standards for Judicial AI (Tesis II.2o.C.9 K)
D0YWuWHjUKj45sISuZmW.resumen: In validating the use of AI for judicial calculations, the Tribunal Colegiado (collegial court), through an exercise of judicial restraint, established four 'minimum elements' mandatory for guaranteeing human rights: proportionality, data protection, transparency (explainability), and non-delegable human oversight.
D0YWuWHjUKj45sISuZmW.hechos: Stemming from the same Recurso de Queja (petition for review) 212/2025 in which AI was used to assess a constitutional guarantee, the Court warned that absent secondary legislation, deploying these tools without safeguards would be risky. Therefore, it developed a specific tesis (jurisprudential standard) to define the methodological and ethical framework that any juzgador (judge) who decides to rely on artificial intelligence must follow, grounded in international standards (UNESCO, European Union).
D0YWuWHjUKj45sISuZmW.elementoIA: The ruling defines AI governance protocols: it prohibits its use for 'legal reasoning' (interpretation of legal provisions), limiting it to 'numerical reasoning' or auxiliary functions, and requires auditing 'prompts' and protecting personal data in the expediente (case file).

o1LJhZ9OjpenfPkWysq1.nombre: Case on Penal Taxativity in the Definition of AI (Quintana Roo)
o1LJhZ9OjpenfPkWysq1.resumen: The Federal Executive challenged Article 20 Bis of the Quintana Roo Criminal Code (Código Penal), which increases penalties when AI is used to commit crimes. The central argument was that the definition of AI was ambiguous and violated the principle of penal taxativity. The Supreme Court Plenary (Pleno de la SCJN - Mexican Supreme Court of Justice Plenary) dismissed the action (the norm survives) after failing to reach the qualified majority of 8 votes for its invalidation (vote 5 in favor of invalidation, 4 against).
o1LJhZ9OjpenfPkWysq1.hechos: On April 10, 2024, Quintana Roo published Decree 211, amending Article 20 Bis of its Criminal Code. This article establishes an increase in penalty (up to half more) for whoever uses AI as a means to commit crimes and legally defines 'Artificial Intelligence'. The Federal Legal Counsel promoted an Action for Unconstitutionality (Acción de Inconstitucionalidad - Mexican constitutional challenge), arguing that the definition ('simulating human capacities', 'creativity', etc.) was imprecise, generating legal uncertainty about what conduct would be sanctioned, violating Articles 14 and 16 of the Mexican Constitution.
o1LJhZ9OjpenfPkWysq1.elementoIA: The debate centered on the technical versus legal definition of AI as set forth in the law: 'the capacity of systems... to simulate human capacities such as reasoning, learning, creativity...'. The Court analyzed whether this technological description is sufficient to comply with the strict principle of legality in criminal matters (taxativity).
